title.narrative: Tonle Sap Poverty Reduction and Smallholder Development Program (Asian Development Fund Loan)

description.narrative: The Tonle Sap Poverty Reduction and Smallholder Development Project will foster community-driven development through investments in productivity improvement, rural infrastructure, and capacity development in 196 communes in the provinces of Banteay Meanchey, Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, and Siem Reap. The Project will assist the Government in creating (i) community driven development through a commune block grant with the following three subcomponents: (a) improving rural infrastructure supporting agricultural productivity; (b) improving capacity of smallholder farmers; (c) strengthened commune project management capacity; (ii) enabling Environment for Agriculture Productivity and Diversification with the following subcomponents: (a) improving agricultural policy environment; (b) increasing availability of and access to quality seeds; and (c) increasing access to agricultural information and market data; and (iii) Effective Project Management.

With additional financing: MAFF estimated average yields (DS & WS) across Cambodia was 3.55 tons/ha, 3.29 tons/ha, 3.31 tons/ha and 3.49 tons/ha for 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2023 respectively. Achieved: 101% Data Source: Sample crop cuts using FAO methodology

Marketed farm and off-farm products increased by 25%. Progress/Status: Original project: - Two agriculture stations and Warehouses (Balang in Kampong Thom province; and Tuek Vil in Siem Reap province) produced certified rice seeds. 187 tons of rice certified seeds (CS) had been produced by the two stations so far and 200 tons of CS bought from RSPGs (BMC: 3, SRP: 9 & KPT:8) as of 31 Dec 2017. Since 2018 the two stations have purchased 198 tons of CS from four RSPGs, and in the case of Balang station this was achieved through contract farming agreements.
- 35 rice seed producer groups (RSPGs) successfully formed and assisted with a total membership of 831 including 333 women. The RSPGs have collectively produced 3,883 tons of good rice seeds and collectively sold 2,739 tons to farmers (67 tons to LIG members).
- 1,616 on-farm demonstrations conducted, which includes 1,019 for crops (rice: 588, vegetables/mushroom: 293, and cash crops: 138), 482 for livestock (poultry/chicken/duck: 312, pig: 139, and feed/ forage: 31) and 115 for aquaculture (fish: 60 and frog: 55).
With additional financing: Too early to assess -According the TSSD-AF baseline survey with total 1,546 target HH in 2022, the average income (selling amount) of TG HH from rice selling was US$1,305 (42% of total TG HH), cash crop was US$1,751 (22% of total TG HH), livestock was US$758 (24% of total TG HH), and vegetable US$465 (7% of total TG HH). - Total 64% of total rice produced volume was sold by TG HH in 2020.
The end-line survey found that marketed farm and off-farm products increased by 27%. (in 2019, the ratio was 63% increased to 90% in 2023) Achieved: 108%. Data Source: Household and commune surveys Actual value:

Diversified farming systems reduce share of household income from rice by 20% Achievement: 18 Progress/Status: Original project: - There was an increase in the proportion of households growing cash crops from 12% to 18% with the most popular crops being cassava followed by maize and cashew. In the case of cassava the productivity increased by 150% but for other crops there was no apparent increase. - Average income per household from selling cash crops increased from US$ 1,458 to US$ 2,269. - There was a slight increase in the proportion of households engaged in livestock production from 68% to 73%. - The proportion of households engaged in off-farm income increased from 26% to 30%.
With additional financing: - According TSSD-AF baseline survey, in 2020, there was 20% of target (TG) HH had one source of income, 44% of TG HH had 2 sources of income, 27% with 3 sources of income and 8% of TG HH had more than 3 sources of income. - In 2020, the income of TG HH from rice was 45%, cash crops were 27%, vegetable was 6%, from livestock 21%, and aquaculture was 1%. The end-line survey indicated that the share of income from rice decreases from 44% in 2019 to 21% in 2023. Incomes from agriculture activities other than rice - including cash crop, vegetables farming, and petty trade have increased remarkably.
Achieved: 115%. Data Source: LIG and MIG records in project communes

Output: Original project: Community Driven Development through a commune block grant (a. Improving Rural Infrastructure, b. Improved capacity of smallholder farmers, c. Improved Commune Capacity for project management) / Overall project: Rural productive infrastructure and livelihood improved with capacity in disaster risk management enhanced Indicator: Original project: 90 km of rural roads and small-scale irrigation and drainage facilities covering 2,500 ha farmland improved (target exceeded; 417 km of laterite and earth roads have been rehabilitated and irrigation systems have been improved to service 55,000 ha including 5,000 ha of dry season crops).
Overall project: At least 867 km of rural roads improved, including 450 km of roads that contribute to DRR and small-scale irrigation provided to cover 11,000 ha farmland to support at least two crops per year.
Overall project: At least 25% of unskilled workers for the construction/rehabilitation of project-supported infrastructure are women (baseline: 25% in 2016) Achievement: 466.6 Progress/Status: Original project: Completed. 417 km of laterite roads rehabilitated and irrigation systems have been improved to service 55,000 ha including 5,000 ha of dry season crops.
Overall project:
a. A total of 579 rural infrastructure subprojects were initially identified in target communes across the seven provinces, excluding the two core subprojects identified during the PPTA in 2017 that have already completed construction. Out of these subprojects there were 244 selected based on the required selection criteria specified in the PAM by SSP6 team (including two pilot subprojects during TRTA) together with PSTs; the subprojects comprise 197 rural road (1 Asphalt concrete, 42 concrete, 54 DBST, 21 SBST, 61 laterites, 1 earth, 12 bitumen road, 5 gravel road) subprojects and 47 irrigation sub-projects (43 canals, 2 Reservoir and 2 dams).
b. Topographic surveys have been completed for 225 of these sub-projects, detailed engineering designs (DEDs) have been completed for 162 subprojects and 147 (incl. 2 pilot subprojects) subprojects have social safeguard report and environment safeguard reports approved and disclosed
c. A total 147 subprojects (116 rural roads, 31 irrigation schemes) awarded the contracts. All subprojects have completed construction and 75 subprojects (incl. 2 pilot) have passed their warranty period (contract closed), that comprised 116 rural road subprojects with a total length of 354.33 km and 31 irrigation subprojects that will enable dry season cropping on an area of 7,108 hectares and paddy field-village access laterite-covered road of 112.27 Km in total length.
d. The project has renovated a total length of 466.6 km of community disaster risk reduction roads against the target of 450 km (104%) and 31 small-scale canals to irrigate 7,108 ha of paddy field for two crops/year against the target of 6,000ha (118% ) have been constructed. A total amount of $33.9 million has been utilized for rural infrastructure ($27.3 million for rural roads; and $6.6 million for small-scale irrigations).
e. Each of 147 subprojects, Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Committee has been established and nine provincial training courses on O&M were organized for 626 committee members (80 women, or 13%) of completed subprojects.
f. A total of 21 contract variations were made for 20 subprojects with an additional cost of $0.66 million to (i) repair 16 subprojects that were damaged by the 2020 and 2022 floods; and (ii) improve the design of 5 subprojects to bring more benefits to the communities. Due to budget concerns, the mission recommended NCDDS to stop conducting any new contract variations with additional costs and avoid any new subprojects with immediate effects.
h. During 2020, a total of 341 unskilled laborers, included 122 women (36%) were employed in construction of civil work for the subprojects. In 2021 total 233 unskilled laborers were employed (including 93 women (40%). In 2022 , total 621 unskilled laborers were employed (including 215 women (35%). In 2023, a total 959 unskilled laborers were employed (including 345 women (36%). In the first quarter of 2024, a total of 82 unskilled laborers were employed including 33 women (40%). Data Source: Quarterly progress reports
